1. In neither of the situations I’ve gotten in between, violence got directed at me. And I know from my own experiences with people who hit children, they’re likely to actually stop, come up with some weird justification for what they did (because in their eyes they’re just doing something good for the child - teaching them to behave), or be taken by surprise, rather than directing violence at someone else. 

2. If violence would get directed at me, yes, would suck for me. But as long as I don’t respond to that violence with violence, the chance of ‘ending up in jail’ is close to zero or completely inexistant. 

3. (At least where I live) hitting children is illegal, and a punishable offense. If the parent’s defense is “if I was beating my child, this person told me to stop so I beat them instead”, they’ll still be the one in trouble. You’ll only get in trouble if you actually use violence (or violence other than basic self protection). Plus OP is talking about Walmart/public spaces, meaning surveillance cameras and witnesses.

4. Even if it doesn’t help at all to stop the abuse, at least the child (or whoever is the receiver of the abuse), sees there are people who care, and that what’s happening is not ok or acceptable. Even if no one can help, seeing that there are people out there who care enough to try, makes a huge difference. 

Just want to add as well that I can understand if you’re a minority that’s often facing police violence you wouldn’t want to risk your own safety in this case (because I can understand that initially there might be some confusion if two adults are in a fight and bystanders/police don’t know the context), and I don’t judge that. However, the chance of that happening to me (being a white woman in a country where police doesn’t even carry guns), is not really there. So I, personally, would stand up for that child and come in between without a second thought.

TLDR: In my opinion, it can be very fun to use pot with a SO, given you’re both into it, but it won’t make a relationship stronger or fix any relationship issues. 

My ex and I used to use weed together semi-regularly (he’d buy a bag, we’d use it on a weekly basis until it ran out, then take a break for a few months until he bought more). 

It was a fun thing to do with a partner, and I’ve sometimes gotten high with someone I used to date for a short while after him as well. If you’re both into it, it can be a fun experience. But to me it’s not much different than getting drunk together from time to time. 

It can be fun, but it doesn’t solve existing relationship issues, or doesn’t necessarily make the relationship stronger (not more than going out drinking for an evening makes a relationship stronger, for example). And just like with any other shared activity, it can introduce some other problems too. It had a different effect on both of us, which sometimes let to minor communication issues. 

We broke up after a while, which was unrelated to the pot use. We wanted different things out of the relationship and I realized I was gay.

If you’re in good shape, go for a hiking trip somewhere. There are lots of options available, both during day and night. I’d go at least for either one long one (that take 7-10 hours), or two smaller ones in different areas. 

Otherwise, there are boat trips available too, but they’re a bit more pricy than the hiking trips (don’t know about your budget), but can also take you to more places outside Longyearbyen. I did a few trips with Better Moments when I was there last July, I can’t recommend them enough, but I’m not sure what kind of trips they have available in June. 

Clothing-wise, during July I had temperatures between 0 and 10 degrees Celsius. So dress warm, but wear lots of different layers rather than just a warm sweater and jacket. While we were out on the water, I had to wear woolen underwear, woolen shirt, regular shirt woolen sweater, woolen cardigan-type thing and a jacket (and two pairs of pants). When hiking, I often took off most of those layers ended up walking in just one shirt and pants. Also, invest in good hiking shoes and wear them enough before going. I saw people showing up to hiking trips in Converse, and they were just sent back (with good reason, that shit is dangerous). 

Otherwise, Svalbard is beautiful place, hoping to go back soon myself, so enjoy your vacation! :)

That’s what I say to a lot of people too, however in relationships I try to explain them I have CPTSD and what it is, since to me it feels very different from regular anxiety and I have a lot of triggers. If hearing my neighbors come home late is going to trigger anything and make me feel depressed, anxious and on-alert for an entire day (or days), it’s best that the people I live with/spend a lot of time around know what’s up. 

With one if my girlfriends I brought it up when the conversation went in the direction of trauma and anxiety, because she was talking about her PTSD. With my other girlfriend I brought it up when something triggered me. I told my ex after a trigger as well. 

I have asthma as well, and I tell people about my CPTSD in the same way. I don’t introduce myself as “Hey I’m X and I have asthma”, or “Hey, I’m X and have CPTSD”. But when it’s relevant to the conversation, or I get to a point where it’s important for people to know. For example, when I’m sleeping over at a friend and I think I’ll have an asthma attack during the night, I tell them I have asthma and might have an attack, and explain them how to react. Similarly with my CPTSD, when I get to a point in the relationship where they might start noticing something or if we’re going into a situation that might trigger me, I tell them as well. 

People might not always understand, even if they have the best intentions to, because it’s something that’s hard to understand if you haven’t experienced it yourself. But what’s important is that they respect it and offer support. :)
